subject: general
question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

“Call the first witness,” said the judge.

options.text: The judge asked if they would call the first witness.
The judge said that the first witness should be called.
The judge ordered that called the first witness.
The judge ordered them to call the first witness.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** “Call the first witness,” said the judge.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Sentence Type:** The quoted speech is an imperative sentence (a command).
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Because a judge is issuing a command in an official capacity, the reporting verb "said" changes to "ordered".
 
 
 
• **Verb Conversion:**
 
 
• In imperative sentences, the direct verb ("Call") is changed into an infinitive ("to call").
 
 
 
• **Object Introduction:**
 
 
• An implied object ("them") is introduced after the reporting verb to make the sentence structurally complete and clear (i.e., "ordered them").
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The judge ordered them to call the first witness.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** The judge asked if they would call the first witness.

 
 
• Incorrectly treats the imperative command as a Yes/No question by using "asked if".
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** The judge said that the first witness should be called.
 
 
• Converts the sentence into a passive construction using a modal verb ("should be called"), completely ignoring the standard infinitive rule for reporting imperative sentences.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The judge ordered that called the first witness.
 
 
• Grammatically incorrect. The conjunction "that" directly followed by the past tense verb "called" does not form a coherent clause.
